claims.text: A securityContext can be set on a Pod (PodSecurityContext, applies to all its containers) or on a container (SecurityContext); it defines the user the process runs as and privilege and access settings.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tasks > Configure a Security Context for a Pod or Container

claims.text: When a container image's configuration names no USER, the container's process runs as root (UID 0), unless the manifest sets runAsUser.
claims.source_hint: docs.docker.com: Dockerfile reference (USER: default is root); kubernetes.io: Configure a Security Context (runAsUser)

claims.text: runAsUser sets the UID the container's entrypoint runs as, overriding the image's USER; when absent the image metadata's user is used.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: API reference SecurityContext.runAsUser (Defaults to user specified in image metadata if unspecified)

claims.text: With runAsNonRoot: true the kubelet validates the user at runtime before starting the container and fails to start it if it would run as UID 0; it does not change the user.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: API reference SecurityContext.runAsNonRoot; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/security-context.txt

claims.text: With runAsNonRoot: true and an image whose USER is a non-numeric name and no runAsUser, the kubelet refuses: 'image has non-numeric user (nobody), cannot verify user is non-root'; it does not resolve names from the image's user list.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/security-context.txt; kubernetes kubelet source verifyRunAsNonRoot (kuberuntime_container_linux / security_context_others)

claims.text: A container refused by the runAsNonRoot check is not started; the Pod shows STATUS CreateContainerConfigError and the reason in status.containerStatuses[].state.waiting.message. Also applies when runAsUser is 0.
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/security-context.txt; kubernetes.io: Debug Pods (CreateContainerConfigError)

claims.text: allowPrivilegeEscalation: false prevents a process from gaining more privileges than its parent (sets no_new_privs), e.g. via a setuid file owned by root; it is always true for a privileged: true container (essentially root on the node) or one with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, a broad administrative capability.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Configure a Security Context (allowPrivilegeEscalation: controls the no_new_privs flag)

claims.text: Linux capabilities divide root's privileges into units (e.g. CAP_CHOWN); the runtime grants each container a small default set; a non-root process cannot use all of them directly, but they stay within reach of the container until dropped; drop: ["ALL"] removes the set whatever the user.
claims.source_hint: man7.org capabilities(7); kubernetes.io: Configure a Security Context (Set capabilities for a Container)

claims.text: seccomp filters the system calls a process may make; seccompProfile type RuntimeDefault applies the container runtime's default seccomp profile, the runtime's own set of allowed and blocked system calls.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Tutorials > Restrict a Container's Syscalls with seccomp (RuntimeDefault); Configure a Security Context (seccomp)

claims.text: Fields set in both the Pod's and the container's securityContext take the container's value; capabilities and allowPrivilegeEscalation exist only in the container SecurityContext; runAsNonRoot and runAsUser exist in both.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Configure a Security Context (settings in container securityContext override Pod-level); API reference PodSecurityContext vs SecurityContext

claims.text: Without user namespaces (Kubernetes default, hostUsers true), UID 0 in a container is UID 0 on the node and all containers on a node share its kernel; user namespaces (hostUsers: false) map container users to other node UIDs.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Workloads > Pods > User Namespaces (without them, root in container is root on host)

claims.text: A file a root process in a container creates in a hostPath-mounted node folder is owned by root (UID 0) on the node.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Volumes (hostPath: files created on the host are writable only by root / security risks)

claims.text: Opinion: when a process does not need root or kernel powers, run it as a numeric non-root user with runAsNonRoot, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped and RuntimeDefault seccomp, so a taken-over process can do less.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Pod Security Standards (restricted profile controls); Configure a Security Context
